task: Fix the data pipeline backpressure failure after the consumer batch size was increased.

candidate_memories.content: Pipeline consumers are dropping messages when the batch size exceeds the broker's max fetch bytes setting.
Consumer batch size must not exceed the broker's max.fetch.bytes setting of 52428800 bytes (50MB).
The batch size was increased from 1000 to 5000 records without checking the broker's max fetch limit.
When increasing consumer batch size, always verify the broker's max fetch bytes setting matches.
Dropping occurs only at peak load when individual messages are large; small-message batches are unaffected.
The message broker is Apache Kafka 3.5 running on a 6-node cluster.
Session 3 note: the data team added a new consumer group for the analytics pipeline.
Old lesson: consumer lag was the primary metric for backpressure detection before drop monitoring was added.
The Kafka cluster is managed by Confluent Cloud with default broker settings.
Session 8 note: consumer group rebalancing was optimized to reduce rebalance duration.
Old pipeline guide: the batch size was 500 records in the original consumer design.
Producer and consumer batch sizes must be tested against broker limits before increasing in production.
Session 12 note: a new dead-letter topic was added for messages that fail processing.
The pipeline processes 2 million messages per day with an average message size of 8KB.
A throughput test in session 6 showed the pipeline handled 10,000 messages/second with the old batch size.
The consumer uses the Confluent Kafka Go client with manual offset commits.
When configuring consumer batch sizes, account for both record count and byte size limits.
Session 10 note: the monitoring team added consumer lag alerts with a 5-minute threshold.
Old Kafka guide: the default max.fetch.bytes was 1MB before the broker was reconfigured for large messages.
Messages are serialized with Avro and the schema is registered in the Confluent Schema Registry.
